## Definition

**Ordinal data** have a meaningful order or ranking, but the intervals between values are not necessarily equal. We know the relative position but not the exact distance between values.

## Characteristics

| Property | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| Order | Values can be ranked |
| Unequal intervals | Distance between ranks varies |
| No true zero | Zero is often arbitrary |
| Relative position | Know "more than" but not "how much more" |

## Examples

| Variable | Values | Why Ordinal |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| Race position | 1st, 2nd, 3rd | Gap between 1st and 2nd ≠ gap between 2nd and 3rd |
| Likert scale | 1-5 agreement | "Agree" to "Strongly agree" may not equal "Neutral" to "Agree" |
| Pain rating | None, Mild, Moderate, Severe | Intervals not standardised |
| Education | GCSE, A-Level, Degree | Not equally spaced |

## Appropriate Statistics

| Statistic | Use |
|-----------|-----|
| Median | Middle value |
| Mode | Most frequent value |
| Percentiles | Relative standing |
| Spearman's rho | Correlation |
| Mann-Whitney U | Between-groups comparison |
| Wilcoxon | Within-groups comparison |

## The Likert Scale Debate

Likert scales (e.g., 1 = Strongly Disagree to 5 = Strongly Agree) are technically ordinal, but often treated as interval:

| Argument | Position |
|----------|----------|
| Strict | Non-parametric tests only |
| Pragmatic | Parametric tests are robust |
| Common practice | Often treated as interval |

**Recommendation:** With multiple Likert items summed into a scale, treating as interval is often acceptable.

## Ordinal vs. Interval

```
Ordinal: Runners finish 1st, 2nd, 3rd
         1st ●──?──● 2nd ──?──● 3rd
         (gaps unknown)

Interval: Temperature 10°C, 20°C, 30°C
          10°●──10──●20°──10──●30°
          (equal 10° intervals)
```

## DataLab Connection

At **Sixth Sense**, confidence ratings (1-7) are ordinal—we can't assume the difference between 1 and 2 equals the difference between 6 and 7. Use non-parametric tests or acknowledge the limitation.
